title: Current accounts in Germany: providers newcomers commonly choose
description: Branch banks and app-only banks compared for people who have just arrived in Germany: Commerzbank, Postbank, N26, Wise, bunq, Revolut and Tomorrow.
html:
Every bank has its strengths. The short profiles below describe well-known providers that newcomers to Germany commonly choose; check the current conditions on their websites before you decide. The EC Assets Bank Account, which comes with the {{product}}, is described on its own page.

Commerzbank

Commerzbank is one of Germany's largest branch banks. Its current account suits people who want a traditional bank with a solid app and the option of walking into a branch.

Conditions change regularly; new-customer offers and monthly fees are published on the bank's website.

Visit Commerzbank

Wise

Wise started as a low-cost transfer service and now offers a multi-currency account with a card. It is quick to set up, the app is available in many languages, and it is a practical choice for people who move money between countries.

Visit Wise

N26

N26 is a fully licensed German bank with a German IBAN. The account is opened in the app in a few minutes, comes with a virtual card and English-speaking support, and is a popular choice among people arriving from abroad.

Visit N26

Postbank

Postbank, part of Deutsche Bank, is a large retail bank with branches across the country and mobile banking. A good fit if you value a physical branch nearby.

Visit Postbank

Bunq

Bunq is one of the larger European app-only banks, with personal and business accounts, real-time payments, multiple currencies, shared expenses and virtual cards. A German IBAN is available.

Visit Bunq

Revolut

Revolut is one of Europe's largest digital banks, covering spending, saving, investing and borrowing in one app.

The account is opened in the app in a few minutes.

Visit Revolut

Tomorrow

Tomorrow is a mobile bank with a focus on sustainability: real-time payments, a clear spending overview and a Visa card, with part of the revenue directed to environmental projects.

The account is opened on a smartphone in a few minutes.

Visit Tomorrow

Provider descriptions are for orientation only. EC Assets receives no commission from the banks listed here.

From our product pages: what a current account gives you

Banking that moves with you

  • Three free ATM withdrawals a month in Germany and across the EU.
  • Activate your digital debit card on arrival and use it anywhere.
  • Physical card on request for a small delivery fee.
  • Manage your money whenever and wherever you like: salary, card payments, direct debits and more.
  • Get your visa essentials and your Bank Account in one go with the {{product}}.

Why a German account belongs at the top of your list

Sort out your account before the first rent is due

A German current account (Girokonto) is one of the first things you need after arrival. It receives your monthly Blocked Account payouts and pays for insurance, rent and everyday costs.

The EC Assets Bank Account is included in the {{product}}. If you would rather use another bank, the overview below shows the most common choices among newcomers.

Prefer a branch bank?

  • The large German retail banks combine branches for in-person service with online banking for everything else
  • As fully licensed German banks they issue a German IBAN, which simplifies contracts and payroll
  • Most offer both a Girocard and a debit card. The Girocard is a German speciality accepted in almost every shop, so having both gives you the most flexibility

We compare the most common choices in our guide.

What is a Girocard?

The Girocard is a German debit card issued by banks; it is not a credit card. Older names for it are EC-Karte and Maestro card. It matters most in smaller towns, where some shops and restaurants take only cash or Girocard.

Our guide to finance and banking in Germany covers the banking system, account types and transfers in more depth. You may also want to read about international transfers to your Blocked Account or your German bank account.

Have your documents ready

Opening an account usually requires your passport and proof of your German address, such as the registration certificate. Some banks also ask for a copy of your residence permit.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a German bank account?

You need a European current account to receive the monthly transfers from your Blocked Account. The Blocked Account itself cannot be used for daily spending, rent or direct debits.

How do I open an account in Germany?

Online with most providers, or in a branch of any German bank.

Which account does EC Assets recommend?

The EC Assets Bank Account is included in the {{product}} and linked to your Blocked Account. If you prefer another provider, any of the banks above works; the choice is yours.

Which account can receive my Blocked Account payouts?

Any current account at a European bank. With the EC Assets Bank Account the payouts arrive automatically, without entering any bank details.

What is a current account?

The account used for day-to-day money: card payments, direct debits such as rent, ATM withdrawals and incoming salary. It is what most people mean when they say "bank account".
